notes:
- Write a new activity: The Activity tab's heading now carries a compose button that opens a Material 3 sheet for a text post. Markdown, a live counter and AniList's own 5-character floor; the stored post is inserted at the top of the feed the moment it lands, without a refetch. Only your own profile offers it, because a text activity is written to your account.
- The Info page uses AniList's banner: The hero's backdrop was measured from a crossfade that had no size and two children that all used matchParentSize, so it measured to zero and neither the banner nor the poster drew. The crossfade now fills the hero and the wide banner crossfades in over the key visual as a full-bleed, top-anchored crop instead of a thin strip.
- Deleting a comment sticks: A delete used to be trusted unconditionally, so even a refused delete removed the row and the comment came back on the next open. The mutation's own confirmation is now required, the last-closed thread's snapshot drops the reply when the answer lands after the sheet is gone, and the chat window's visible-row count shrinks with the list.
- Global no longer hides Messages: The opt-in Global chip used to sit between Friends and Messages and pushed Messages past the right edge of a row that scrolls without saying so. Global is now the last chip and animates in when the setting is turned on, and a conversation opened from a Global row starts with a clean reply box.
- Edit reply in comments: Replies to comments can now be edited with the full composer: the same header, preview, format bar, counter and GIF picker that writing a new comment uses. Edit mode starts from the existing comment's text, and changes are saved back to the comment thread.
- Comment composer bottom-row icons: The icons in the composer's bottom row were consistently 20dp inside their 48dp touch targets, making 24dp vectors look undersized. All glyphs now render at the vector's own 24dp default and the same 48dp target size as the rest of the bar, so they touch-target and visually match the other controls.
- Reply from a friend's activity: Tapping a person's name in the Activity or Global feed now opens a fresh conversation with that author, rather than showing the viewer's own messages. The inbox is fetched and a blank reply box is shown, so the reader can write the first message. A reader cannot message themselves - the server would reject it and the UI disables it.
- View messages from friend activity: From a friend's activity row (Friends or Global feed), the author row now carries a message entry point. Tapping it opens a conversation with that author, even if no prior messages exist. This works the same way as opening from the Messages tab: a thread is assembled from both halves of the inbox, with a reply box underneath.
- Message threads mirror AniList's: Opening a private message now loads that message's own AniList thread - the message and every reply, from either account - instead of matching whatever the inbox and notification pages happened to contain. Replies post into the same thread with SaveActivityReply, which is the mutation the site's own message page uses, so a private exchange reads the same as a public one and nothing is sent as a fresh top-level message. A message from two years ago still shows the whole conversation.
- GIF search returns results again: Safebooru filters on rating:safe, and the picker was asking for rating:general - a value the site does not know, which matches nothing and answers an empty page for every query. The request now uses the same spelling the response's own rating field carries, so searches for a character or a show return the catalogue again.
- Camera photos can be attached: HEIC and HEIF photos were being refused as unsupported image types before the app reached its own re-encode step, so the one format an Android camera writes could not be attached at all. Those two are now accepted and converted to JPEG, and the converted file is checked against the host's size limit before it is uploaded.
- The composer's bar fits its controls: The format controls now take a full row of their own, with the counter and the Post button on a second row, instead of sharing width with them. More controls are visible at once, the Post button never scrolls away, and a poster-sized GIF tile falls back to the provider's still image rather than drawing a 27-megapixel frame in a 104dp cell.
